title: U.S. House · Georgia's 12th District
area: East Georgia, including Augusta, Columbia County, and Statesboro.

context.text: Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rate this race Solid Republican, Sabato's Crystal Ball rates it Safe Republican, and Decision Desk rates it Likely Republican.

summary.text: Rick Allen has represented Georgia's 12th Congressional District since 2015. Before Congress, he founded and ran R. W. Allen & Associates, an Augusta-based construction firm, after earning a B.S. in building construction from Auburn University.

background.text: Born in Augusta, Georgia, in 1951; graduated from Auburn University in 1973 with a B.S. in building construction.
Worked as an estimator, project administrator, and assistant to the president at an Augusta construction firm before founding his own company, R. W. Allen & Associates, Inc., in 1976.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce and as Vice Chair of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

record.text: Serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), and also sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

candidates.name: Ceretta Smith
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16 Democratic primary runoff over Traci George, 55.8%

summary.text: Ceretta Smith is a Grovetown city councilwoman, Army veteran, and retired federal labor-union official running for Georgia's 12th Congressional District. She served nearly a decade as an Army medic and 25 years as a federal employee and union leader with the American Federation of Government Employees.

background.text: Served nearly a decade as a U.S. Army medic, including a posting in Germany.

Worked 25 years as a federal employee, rising through leadership of the American Federation of Government Employees, including as Georgia State Council President and National Fair Practices Coordinator.
Serves as a city councilwoman in Grovetown, Georgia, where she has lived for 20 years; created a citywide literacy initiative distributing books to children.

priorities.text: Says she is running "to restore trust in government by putting people before party" and will "work across the aisle."
Campaign centers on economic opportunity: creating jobs, lowering costs, supporting small businesses and family farmers, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Says she will work to improve access to affordable healthcare and education and to ensure veterans and rural communities get needed resources.

positions.summary: Says she will work to improve access to affordable healthcare.
